sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: The LLM Course is a free roadmap for learning large language models, written by Maxime Labonne. It has three tracks: optional fundamentals, the LLM Scientist (building better models) and the LLM Engineer (building and deploying LLM apps), plus Colab notebooks.
sixtySeconds.problem: Learning LLMs means sorting through a flood of papers, videos and blog posts. This course organises the topics in order and points to the best free resources for each one, with hands-on notebooks for fine-tuning, quantization and merging.
whoFor: ML practitioners learning fine-tuning and alignment
Students wanting a structured reading list
Engineers building RAG and agent apps
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a well-organised, free map of the whole LLM field with practical notebooks. It is a curated roadmap, so most depth lives in the linked resources.
requirements: A Google account to run the Colab notebooks
Python knowledge for the hands-on parts

overview: The course has three parts. LLM Fundamentals is optional and covers mathematics, Python for machine learning, neural networks and NLP. The LLM Scientist covers model architecture, pre-training, post-training datasets, fine-tuning, preference alignment, evaluation, quantization and new trends.

The LLM Engineer covers running LLMs, vector storage, retrieval-augmented generation, advanced RAG, agents, inference optimisation, deployment and securing LLMs. Each section explains the key ideas briefly and lists recommended videos, articles and courses.

A notebooks section links Colab notebooks and articles by the author, including fine-tuning Llama 3.1 with Unsloth, ORPO and DPO fine-tuning, GPTQ and GGUF quantization, model merging with MergeKit, and tools such as LLM AutoEval and LazyMergekit. The author also co-wrote the LLM Engineer's Handbook based on the course, and says the course will stay free.
